abstract: Maintains archaeological artifact handling protocols and deep-water robotic retrieval history
system_message:
You are State underwater archaeologist (SUA). The State underwater archaeologist (SUA) is responsible for maintaining archaeological artifact handling protocols and logging deep-water robotic retrieval history, alongside tracking onboard conservation facilities.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Maintains archaeological artifact handling protocols and deep-water robotic retrieval history（HERITAGE）
information_points.content:
SUA-HERITAGE-UW1：Pelagic Oceanic Recovery Alliance maintains formal ratification of the UNESCO-aligned in situ artifact extraction protocol, verifying an active marine heritage conservation protocol of true. Additionally, abyssal archaeology records for operations below 500 m depth during the past 48 months reflect an ROV deep-water artifact recovery count of 22 recoveries.
SUA-HERITAGE-O7V：For Caledonian Deep-Ocean Heritage Group, the underwater cultural heritage permit docket confirms that formal ratification of the UNESCO-aligned in situ artifact extraction protocol is in place, demonstrating an active marine heritage conservation protocol of true. Furthermore, according to the abyssal archaeology logbook, their operations below 500 m depth during the past 48 months document an ROV deep-water artifact recovery count of 16 recoveries.
SUA-HERITAGE-79T：Nordic Abyssal Survey Consortium holds formal ratification of the UNESCO-aligned in situ artifact extraction protocol, establishing an active marine heritage conservation protocol of true. Over the past 48 months of operations below 500 m depth, the abyssal archaeology logbook records an ROV deep-water artifact recovery count of 8 recoveries.

information_points.title: Desalination bath logging（CURAT）
information_points.content:
SUA-CURAT-LGO：The conservation staging register indicates that Nordic Abyssal Survey Consortium maintains a passive desalination bath capacity of 1200 L across its vessel wet laboratory stabilization facilities.
SUA-CURAT-61F：Records from the conservation staging register show that Pelagic Oceanic Recovery Alliance has a passive desalination bath capacity of 1600 L within its vessel wet laboratory stabilization setup.
SUA-CURAT-RP6：According to the conservation staging register for vessel wet laboratory stabilization facilities, Caledonian Deep-Ocean Heritage Group provides a passive desalination bath capacity of 2000 L.
